A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same four-modality MM-Fi pose-estimation work. However, v1 references supplementary methods, settings, and results absent from its supplied PDF, whereas v4 includes supplementary Sections 6–7. The main revisions are reliably comparable, but continuity with v1's unavailable supplement cannot be established.

before.justification: v1 reports original MM-Fi pose-estimation experiments, noisy continual-learning evaluations, modality-combination analyses, and component ablations in Tables 1–4 and associated figures.

after.justification: v4 reports original pose-estimation results, computational measurements, and regularization sensitivity experiments, including supplementary MLP-fusion results and qualitative comparisons.

M1.justification: The Shapley/Pearson contribution calculation and modality-specific backbone framework remain, but adaptive re-learning through parameter reinitialization is replaced by Fisher-weighted adaptive weight constraint (AWC) regularization during an initial learning window. v4 also removes the noise identification/separation module and task-adaptive EWC continual-learning procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same MM-Fi dataset, four input modalities, and three activity protocols. v4 removes the distinct continual-learning scenarios involving successive action tasks and raw or unaligned corruption of one modality, substantially narrowing evaluated task and environmental coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds X-Fi for Protocol 3 and HPE-Li for all three protocols while retaining MM-Fi, G-Blending, OGM-GE, AGM, and Modality-level comparisons. The separate continual-learning comparisons against the naive baseline, Co-teaching with EWC, and DivideMix with EWC are removed.

E3.justification: v4 retains the S1 random-split static evaluation and 50 training epochs, but removes the S2 subject split, seven/six-task sequential designs, 20%/40% corruption settings, and task-averaged evaluation metrics. It introduces timing evaluations across two to four modalities and three fusion strategies, alongside controlled AWC coefficient and learning-window sweeps.

E4.justification: v1's noise-separation distributions, task-wise forgetting analysis, and re-learning/NIS/EWC component ablation disappear. v4 adds prediction-distribution analysis, computational-overhead measurements, AWC coefficient ablations, and learning-window sensitivity tests in Figure 3, Table 2, Table 4, and Figure 6. Its supplement also supplies additional qualitative cases.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty across experimental runs. v4 Figure 3 describes the standard deviation of predictions, rather than uncertainty in reported experimental performance.

E6.justification: Numerous retained-table values change. For Protocol 1 concatenation, Table 1 reports baseline MPJPE/PA-MPJPE changing from 52.72/34.14 to 53.87/35.09 mm and the proposed-method row from 49.50/33.65 to 51.16/34.46 mm; the latter represents a changed method. Table 3's best MPJPE fusion changes from all four modalities to RGB+LiDAR. v4 also supplies MLP, timing, and sensitivity results while removing continual-learning results.

T1.justification: v1's reinitialization equation, GMM posterior and clean/noisy-set definitions, and noise-adapted Fisher/EWC formulation are removed. v4 formally defines modality-weighted AWC around epoch-start parameters and adds a linear-fusion decomposition to its regression-scoring argument. The underlying Shapley and Pearson definitions remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion withdraw denoising continual learning and mitigation of catastrophic forgetting as central contributions. They instead emphasize balanced regression through Shapley assessment and early-training AWC without auxiliary learnable parameters, substantially redefining the paper's contribution.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive explanations of why MSE/MAE can misrepresent modality contributions, how Fisher-weighted constraints regulate early learning, and how scoring costs behave. Its modality-fusion interpretation strengthens from limited benefits of weaker modalities to explicit detrimental interference, supported by revised Table 3. Interpretations concerning noise filtering and memory preservation are removed.

D1.justification: v4 newly supplies Adam settings, batch size, weight decay, and learning-rate scheduling. Supplementary Section 6 documents input sequence length, encoder dimensions and strides, projection layers, and detailed fusion implementations, information absent from the supplied v1. These are additional disclosures, not evidence that the retained backbone architecture changed. Both versions still promise code release.

R1.justification: The continual-learning related-work subsection and associated EWC/noisy-stream literature are removed. Positioning shifts toward regression-compatible balancing without auxiliary components, with expanded discussion and citations concerning MMPareto, classifier-guided modulation, adaptive unimodal regulation, and critical learning periods. This changes the relationship to prior research beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Section 3 is reorganized around contribution assessment and AWC, including a substantially expanded classification-versus-regression explanation, while Section 4 loses its two-setting narrative. v4 also includes a structured methods-and-experiments supplement and changes the title and author information.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redesigned around the revised framework, and the continual-learning plots and tables are replaced by prediction-distribution, timing, and sensitivity displays. v4 adds supplementary architecture and qualitative figures and an MLP-results table. The OGM-GE qualitative comparison is retained and renumbered from Figure 6 to Figure 5.

improvement.justification: Compared with the supplied v1, v4 improves reproducibility through concrete architecture and optimizer details and better supports its narrowed balancing contribution through AWC sensitivity and scoring-cost analyses. The benefit is limited: noisy continual-learning validation is withdrawn, and no controlled comparison between AWC and v1's re-learning establishes a superior replacement method. The clearest gain is documentation and assessment of the revised approach.
